Subject: Questions about region anchoring and proof of deletion

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team asked for some clarifications about how Redwood handles region anchoring for Dedicated deployments and what evidence you provide after a tenant deletion. Specific asks: 1) Does Dedicated region-pin prevent snapshot replication to other regions? 2) How are backups handled and can you provide proof (logs/timestamps) that snapshots tied to a tenant are deleted? 3) What about ephemeral caches (prefix cache / KV) — do you scrub those on erase? 4) What's the expected timeline for an evidence package we can present to our auditors?

Can you share a concise playbook or checklist we can review? Attaching our SOC checklist in a follow-up.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Security Operations
Clearline Financial

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@clearline.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about region anchoring and proof of deletion

Elena — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together concise answers and attached a lightweight runbook for our Dedicated customers (redwood_erase_runbook_v2.pdf). Short answers here, and I included an evidence checklist at the end.

1) Region pinning: When a tenant is pinned to a region in Dedicated, we set placement policies so primary data (model inputs/outputs, tenant metadata, and persistent snapshots) are only stored on hosts within that region. We do not replicate persistent snapshots across regions for pinned tenants unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region DR.

2) Backups/snapshots: We keep periodic snapshots per customer per our retention policy. Snapshot lifecycle follows the retention window you agree to; when a tenant delete is requested we execute a snap-deletion workflow that removes index pointers, marks snapshot objects for deletion, and issues a background cleanup job to expunge underlying blocks. We can provide signed deletion records and a CSV of deletion operations (sample_deletion_log.csv).

3) Ephemeral caches: KV/prefix caches and runtime caches are memory/resident and/or on ephemeral local NVMe. Our erase workflow includes a cache eviction phase and a TTL-based scrubbing step. We also rotate ephemeral caches on host reclamation; any residual cached context is garbage-collected and not written to persistent snapshot stores.

4) Evidence timeline: Typical turnaround is 5 business days for the initial evidence package (signed attestations + deletion log + snapshot manifests) and up to 10 business days for forensic artifacts if you request on-host forensic snapshots or host-level attestations.

Attached runbook highlights the steps we perform and the outputs you should expect. If you want, we can run a short tabletop with your auditors and provide sample logs and a redacted CSV for review.

Action items:

- Vanessa: can you produce the signed attestation template and point to the deletion-log sample?
- Ben: please confirm capture of ephemeral cache eviction steps for the runbook.

Thanks,

Hi all — attaching the attestation template we'll sign once deletion completes. A few implementation notes:

- Snap deletion: we mark snapshot manifest IDs as deleted in our metadata service (audit-recorded). The underlying object store supports eventual deletion; we run a final sweep to zero out object manifests and issue a PGP-signed attestation with the manifest IDs and deletion timestamps.
- Geo-lock: when you request a region pin, we disable the cross-region replication pipeline for that tenant at the controller layer and add an irrevocable placement constraint until the pin is removed.
- Host-level wipe: for customers who require host-level evidence, we can provide sanitized host snapshot logs showing scrub timestamps; note that for multi-tenant hosts we only provide tenant-scoped logs (no host full-disk images).

Elena — if you confirm attestation-only is sufficient, we'll proceed to open a deletion run in our ops queue and target a 5-business-day delivery for the package. If you need host-level artifacts, add +5 business days.

Attachments: redwood_attestation_template_v1.pdf (attachment)
